newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Chrysler to announce motor plant site in 60 days.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to announce motor plant site in 60 days.

text.p: Chrysler Corp, the third-ranked automaker in the United States, said it expects to announce within two months the site of its joint venture motor plant it will build with Germany's BMW AG.
"We do not know yet where it will be located. We expect to announce the site of the new plant in 60 days," Chrysler Chairman Robert J. Eaton said here.
Earlier this year, BMW chairman Bernd Pischetsrieder said the $500 million engine plant would probably be set up in Latin America, but he did not identify its location.
The Chrysler president came to Brazil to sign on Thursday an agreement with Parana state government to build a $315 million Dakota truck assembly plant in the southern state.
The new plant, which will build gasoline and diesel-powered Dakota trucks, is expected to start production at the end of the second quarter of 1998.
Chrysler plans to start building 12,000 units a year and will create 400 direct jobs. Total annual capacity is expected to reach 40,000 units.
Eaton said 60 percent of the production will be sold in Brazil and the remainder would be exported to Mercosur countries, mainly Chile and Argentina, and possibly to other Latin American countries.
Eaton also said the company has no plans to build passenger cars in Brazil.
"There are no plans for building passenger cars," he said.

The Brazilian facility will be Chrysler's third unit to be sited in South America. The group is investing $165 million in Argentina to build a plant for production of its utility vehicles Jeep Cherokee and Jeep Grand Cherokee.
Chrysler expects to be able to sell 50,000 cars by year 2,001 in the Mercosur region.
